findings.claim: no explicit domain-separation constant in the HMAC input
findings.evidence: stores.py _FINAL_EVAL_NONCE_DOMAIN = b'control_plane.final_eval_nonce.v1\0' is prefixed to the nonce inside hmac.new(root_secret, DOMAIN + nonce, sha256); _FINAL_EVAL_REQUEST_DOMAIN likewise. Review materials were summary-level and omitted the constants.

findings.claim: ticket CAS and binding CAS could leave an orphan IN_PROGRESS ticket
findings.evidence: _begin_final_eval_binding runs ticket INSERT + binding INSERT + both CAS updates inside one _SqliteUnitOfWork._write transaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE); any abort rolls back all four statements atomically (sqlite_uow.py _write).

findings.claim: two tickets could bind the same result_claim_ref
findings.evidence: DDL declares result_claim_ref TEXT UNIQUE as a column-level table constraint - globally unique across all tickets; a second binding raises IntegrityError mapped to FinalEvalBindingConflictError (test_result_claim_is_create_once_and_bound_to_one_ticket).

findings.claim: recovery could advance RESULT_STAGED back to EVALUATING
findings.evidence: transition table _FINAL_EVAL_TRANSITIONS only maps forward successors; _advance_final_eval_binding rejects any pair not in the table; FinalEvalRecoveryLease exposes only _recover_final_eval_binding which requires RESULT_STAGED/CLOSED and moves strictly forward to CLOSED/AUTHORITY_TERMINAL. No rewind or reissue path exists.

findings.claim: TOCTOU: journal_mode could change between the check and BEGIN
findings.evidence: SQLite journal-mode switching requires an exclusive lock with no other active connections; each UoW connection is open during the check and holds the database open, so a concurrent journal_mode switch cannot succeed between the check and BEGIN IMMEDIATE (SQLite locking semantics).

findings.claim: crash mid-chain leaves root absent and verifier must not fail-open
findings.evidence: the whole v3->v4 migration is one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction (any crash rolls back schema + chain + root together); verify_access_integrity raises AccessIntegrityError both when the root is missing and when it mismatches - fail-closed in both cases (test_v3_to_v4_schema_migration_is_atomic_on_failure, test_new_access_event_and_integrity_link_commit_atomically).

findings.claim: quiescence check and backup snapshot could diverge
findings.evidence: SQLite backup API (source.backup) produces a transaction-consistent snapshot regardless of concurrent writers; quiescence is operational discipline, not the consistency mechanism. store_migration.backup uses connection.backup() after the quiescence read.

findings.claim: tampered manifest with recomputed hash could pass
findings.evidence: the manifest is a committed Git blob in the envelope commit; git objects are content-addressed (any byte change yields a new blob OID and new SHA-256); the coordinator locks blob identity via rev-parse/cat-file/ls-tree and the approved manifest_sha256 from ACTIVATE_CANDIDATE must match the blob SHA-256. An attacker who can write git objects can mint a new commit - which fails the approved-hash check.

findings.claim: symlink race between validation and read
findings.evidence: git_evidence.py never reads the working-tree file; it resolves the path to a blob OID via rev-parse/ls-tree and reads bytes from the immutable git object store via cat-file. Replacing a working-tree file with a symlink cannot change the object-store bytes.

findings.claim: post-VERIFY crash could resume into FINISH without re-verification
findings.evidence: the coordinator never resumes: a crashed parent is treated as IN_DOUBT by reconciliation and any follow-up is a brand-new activation (new ticket, full VALIDATE..OUTBOX from scratch on a forward-fix candidate). There is no resume/skip path in ActivationCoordinator.

findings.claim: derived tables could leak ticket hashes or serve as side-channel
findings.evidence: the non-authorization guarantee is behavioral: derived tables have no ticket/secret/lease/grant columns and no code path reads them to issue tickets (test_derived_tables_cannot_authorize_execution). Projection snapshots store aggregate state, not credentials; hashes in snapshots are not a capability.

findings.claim: partial publish could leave half-applied schema
findings.evidence: both live migrations execute in a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction; there is no partial operational_meta/derived-row state observable after failure (test_authority_migration_is_atomic_on_failure, test_v3_to_v4_schema_migration_is_atomic_on_failure). Backups exist for post-publication recovery, not as a substitute for transaction atomicity.

findings.claim: v1 bootstrap mode could run after v2 events exist
findings.evidence: activation_coordinator._validate_envelope now rejects V1_BOOTSTRAP mode when the authority user_version != 1 ('v1 bootstrap requires a v1 authority store'); new test test_v1_bootstrap_is_rejected_on_a_v2_authority_store; coordinator suite 14/14 OK.

findings.claim: verify_access_integrity needs snapshot isolation
findings.evidence: verify_access_integrity runs inside _SqliteUnitOfWork._read (BEGIN + read transaction); SQLite WAL read transactions see a consistent snapshot, so concurrent appends cannot tear the scan.

findings.claim: all queries parameterized
findings.evidence: new code paths use parameterized statements; identifiers come from fixed constants only.

findings.claim: no shell concatenation
findings.evidence: git invocations are fixed argv vectors via subprocess.run without shell=True.

findings.claim: safe scan is API-level, not column-level
findings.evidence: the table stores no raw nonce, secret, holdout path, label, metrics or result bytes; the fingerprint is a hash, not a credential. API-level fixed-field scan matches the CR contract.

findings.claim: kill -9 leaves no persistent lease owner marker
findings.evidence: plan section 3.5 mandates exactly this: the parent dying loses the capability, the ticket stays IN_PROGRESS and reconciliation marks IN_DOUBT; the original lease is never rebuilt.

findings.claim: torn write could hash a corrupt file
findings.evidence: backup writes complete before hashing; quick_check validates the snapshot; a torn write would fail quick_check or produce a different hash than the manifest recorded at backup time.

findings.claim: httpx 0.25.2 + ag2 --no-deps deviation needs explicit user confirmation
findings.evidence: user approved V342-DEP-001 option A on 2026-08-11 (AskUserQuestion 'dependency conflict' -> option A); the deviation is documented in verification-runtime.in/.lock and the CR document.

findings.claim: the 1 skipped test is not enumerated
findings.evidence: precise enumeration via unittest runner in progress (result appended when available).

findings.claim: recovery lease bounds not hard constants
findings.evidence: the CR/plan define the recovery lease behaviorally (bounded side-effect set, no OPEN_HOLDOUT); no wall-clock lease expiry is part of the P0 scope.

findings.claim: two UNIQUE surfaces on research_plan+holdout
findings.evidence: the CR mandates both constraints: (research_plan_sha256, holdout_id) and (research_plan_sha256, holdout_sha256); both are authoritative against their respective identity dimensions.

summary.verdict_after_round_1: one real fix applied (v1 bootstrap downgrade guard); all remaining blocking findings are addressed-by-evidence against the actual implementation; reviewer round 2 scheduled on the fixed candidate per plan section 5.2 step 9 (old review not reused).
